hints: Represent the amounts in the two containers as a state.
Each legal move has a cost equal to the amount of water moved.
Find a least-cost route from (0,0) to any state whose first amount is x.
analogy: Treat every pair of water levels as a room and each fill, empty or pour as a door with a water cost.
example: With capacities 5 and 3, fill A, pour A to B, empty B, pour A to B, fill A, then pour A to B. A contains 4 and the moved amounts total 19.
algorithm: Run Dijkstra from state (0,0). For each state generate the nonzero fill A/B, empty A/B, and pour A to B or B to A operations. A pour transfers min(source amount, free capacity in destination); its edge cost is that transfer amount, and fill/empty cost the amount added or removed. Store predecessor state and operation on each improvement. Stop when a state with A=x is extracted, then reconstruct and print moves and their total cost. If no such state is reachable, print -1.
correctness: Each graph edge corresponds to exactly one allowed move and has exactly its moved-water cost; every legal sequence corresponds to a path. Dijkstra returns a minimum-cost path because all edge costs are positive. Its predecessor links recover a sequence attaining that cost.
complexity: With capacities a and b, at every reachable state at least one container is empty or full, so there are O(a+b) states and O(a+b) edges. Dijkstra takes O((a+b) log(a+b)) time and O(a+b) space.
